extracted.intended_audience: PARI/GP users; computational number theorists; mathematicians implementing/using elliptic-curve and L-function routines
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and usage/caveats for PARI/GP routines relating to elliptic curves, p-adic invariants, genus-2/hyperelliptic routines and L-functions; includes function semantics, preconditions, precision/performance notes and algorithmic limitations. Useful for developers and researchers computing arithmetic invariants and running numerical experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellmul: complex multiplication handling
rubrics_metrics.description: ellmul(E, z, n) multiplies point z by n; the CM case algorithm assumes characteristic 0 and that the quadratic order to which n belongs has small discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In CM cases results may be limited; library syntax GEN ellmul(GEN E, GEN z, GEN n). Examples show non-CM and CM behaviors, and warnings such as "ellmul: not a complex multiplication in ellmul."

rubrics_metrics.name: ellneg: point negation
rubrics_metrics.description: ellneg(E, z) returns the opposite of the point z on elliptic curve E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ellneg(GEN E, GEN z). Simple semantic behavior; no extra options.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellnonsingularmultiple: minimal nonsingular multiple
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E/Q and P in E(Q), returns [R, n] where n is the least positive integer such that R := [n]P has good reduction at every prime (image in a minimal model is everywhere non-singular).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate returned n; library syntax: GEN ellnonsingularmultiple(GEN E, GEN P). Use when you need a rational point with everywhere-good reduction in the minimal model.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellorder: order-of-point semantics and 'infinite order' sentinel
rubrics_metrics.description: ellorder(E, z, {o}) returns the order of point z on E (finite-field or number-field); returns 0 to indicate infinite order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameter o (optional) historically represented a non-zero multiple of the order of z, preferred format [ord, factor(ord)] — now mostly useless because PARI computes and caches curve cardinality. Use GEN ellorder(GEN E, GEN z, GEN o = NULL). Examples show timing and caching behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellordinate: y-coordinates from x
rubrics_metrics.description: ellordinate(E, x) returns a 0, 1 or 2-component vector containing the y-coordinates of the points of curve E having given x-coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ellordinate(GEN E, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicL: p-adic L-function behavior and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpadicL(E, p, n, {s = 0}, {r = 0}, {D = 1}) returns the value (or r-th derivative) on a character χs of Z_p^* of the p-adic L-function of E/Q twisted by D, given modulo p^n. Representation and output depend on reduction type (supersingular vs ordinary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When E has good supersingular reduction, Lp takes values in Q_p ⊗ H^1_dR(E/Q) and returns components in basis (ω, F(ω)) satisfying (1 − p^{-1}F)^{-2} L_p(E,χ0) = (L(E,1)/Ω)·ω. When E has good ordinary reduction, ellpadicL returns the projection onto the α-eigenspace (unit eigenvalue) of Frobenius. This function is a special case of mspadicL and appears as the first term of mspadic-series; mspadic routines allow different characters, derivatives or quadratic twists at similar cost after precomputation. Library syntax: GEN ellpadicL(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN s = NULL, long r, GEN D = NULL). Examples and checks given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters for ellpadicL: representation of χs
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous characters of Gal(Q(µ_{p^∞})/Q) are identified to Z_p^* via cyclotomic character; in GP a character χs is represented by pair s = (s1,s2) with s1 ∈ Z_p and s2 mod p−1 (or mod 2 for p=2); an integer s denotes (s,s) or χ^s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the representation of characters is necessary to call ellpadicL correctly with twist/derivative parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicfrobenius: Frobenius matrix and precision
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpadicfrobenius(E, p, n) returns the matrix of Frobenius ϕ on crystalline module D_p(E) with respect to basis (ω, η = xω); characteristic polynomial is x^2 − a_p x + p. Matrix is computed to absolute p-adic precision p^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires p > 2 and E with good reduction at p for intended interpretation. Library syntax: GEN ellpadicfrobenius(GEN E, long p, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicheight: cyclotomic p-adic height output and relations
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpadicheight(E, p, n, P, {Q}) returns the cyclotomic p-adic height of rational point P as a vector [f,g] (n p-adic digits); if Q present computes bilinear form (h(P+Q)-h(P-Q))/4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DdR(E) is spanned by ω and η=xω, and ellpadicheight returns coefficients f,g. If P in kernel of reduction and reduction nonsingular, g = −(log_E P)^2 (log_E: formal group logarithm). For short Weierstrass model and P=(x,y), f = log_p(denominator(x)) − 2 log_p(σ(P)). Normalization: heights are twice Silverman's. You may replace p by [p,[a,b]] to get af+bg. For canonical height in ordinary case compute s2 = ellpadics2 once and use ellpadicheight with [p,[1,-s2]]. Library syntax: GEN ellpadicheight0(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN P, GEN Q = NULL). Examples and p-adic regulator notes provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicheightmatrix: p-adic regulator matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpadicheightmatrix(E, p, n, v) given a vector v of points returns the Gram matrix of v with respect to the cyclotomic p-adic height; component (i,j) is ellpadicheight(E,p,n,v[i],v[j]) = [f,g].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like ellpadicheight, p may be replaced by [p,[a,b]] to form af+bg. Library syntax: GEN ellpadicheightmatrix(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN v).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadiclog: formal group logarithm
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpadiclog(E, p, n, P) for P on E(K) in kernel of reduction returns L(t(P)) where t(P) = −x/y is the formal group parameter and L is the formal logarithm attached to the canonical invariant differential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ellpadiclog(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN P). Useful for computing g = −(log_E P)^2 in ellpadicheight when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadics2: unit eigenvector slope for ordinary reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpadics2(E, p, n) (p>2, E/Q ordinary good reduction at p) returns slope s2 of unit eigenvector of ellpadicfrobenius(E,p,n); η + s2 ω is eigenvector for unit eigenvalue of Frobenius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: s2 is unique in p^{-1}Z_p and equals b2/12 − E2/12 (E2: Katz p-adic Eisenstein series). Used to construct canonical p-adic height: compute s2 once and reuse. Library syntax: GEN ellpadics2(GEN E, GEN p, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellperiods: normalized period lattice and quasi-periods
rubrics_metrics.description: ellperiods(w, {flag = 0}) returns normalized periods [W1,W2] of lattice w (or ellinit structure) so τ = W1/W2 has positive imaginary part and lies in SL2(Z) fundamental domain. If flag=1 returns [[W1,W2],[η1,η2]] with quasi-periods satisfying η1W2 − η2W1 = 2iπ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output intended for ellwp, ellzeta, ellsigma, elleisnum; quasi-periods needed only by ellzeta and ellsigma. Library syntax: GEN ellperiods(GEN w, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpointtoz: map point to complex/p-adic parameter z
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpointtoz(E, P) computes complex number z (mod lattice Λ) corresponding to point P (P = [℘_Λ(z), ℘'_Λ(z)]) when E/ C. For E/Q_p with multiplicative reduction returns φ(P) in Q_p or in unramified quadratic extension depending on split/non-split Tate curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If E defined over R and P∈E(R) further constraints 0 ≤ Re(z) < w1 etc. Behavior for multiplicative reduction explained; library syntax zell(GEN E, GEN P, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpow: deprecated alias
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpow(E, z, n) is a deprecated alias for ellmul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ellmul instead; library syntax equivalence noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellrootno: local/global root number computation
rubrics_metrics.description: ellrootno(E, {p}) computes local root number of L-series at place p (p=0 for infinite place); if p omitted returns global root number (sign of functional equation, conjecturally parity of Mordell-Weil rank).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model need not be minimal at p but minimal model speeds computation. Library syntax: long ellrootno(GEN E, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsea: SEA algorithm with tors early-exit parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: ellsea(E, {tors = 0}) computes #E(F_q) using SEA; tors argument provides early-exit when order has small prime factor not dividing tors. If tors non-zero returns 0 as soon as it detects a bad small prime factor not dividing tors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set tors=1 to insist on prime order, tors=2 to allow cofactor power-of-two, etc. SEA not implemented for characteristic ≤7 or tiny q (q ≤ 523), where ellcard fallback used and tors ignored. For q < ~250 generic algorithm is faster. ellsea does not store cardinality in E; ellcard preferred when no almost-prime constraint. seadata package recommended to speed up computation. Library syntax: GEN ellsea(GEN E, ulong tors).

rubrics_metrics.name: cryptocurve idiom: using ellsea with tors for prime-order curve search
rubrics_metrics.description: Example defines cryptocurve(p) that repeatedly samples j-invariants, uses ellsea(E,1) early-exit to find curve of prime order quickly and optionally returns quadratic twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows dramatic speed benefit over running full ellcard; demonstrates setting tors to 1 enables early abort on small factors improving search time. Use when constructing prime-order curves for cryptography.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsearch: selecting curves from elldata
rubrics_metrics.description: ellsearch(N) finds curves in elldata satisfying constraint N: string selects curves by name/isogeny class/conductor; integer vector encodes same constraints; integer selects curves with conductor N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If N codes a full curve name output is [name, [a1..a6], G] where G is Z-basis of free part of Mordell-Weil. If N not full returns vector of matches. Library syntax: GEN ellsearch(GEN N); ellsearchcurve only accepts full curve names.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsigma: Weierstrass sigma function evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: ellsigma(L, {z = x}, {flag = 0}) computes σ(z,L) attached to lattice L (or ellinit structure). If flag=1 computes an arbitrary determination of log(σ(z)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts input L=[ω1,ω2] or E. Series expansion around 0 available. Library syntax: GEN ellsigma(GEN L, GEN z = NULL, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsub: point subtraction
rubrics_metrics.description: ellsub(E, z1, z2) returns the difference of points z1 and z2 on elliptic curve E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple group law helper; library syntax: GEN ellsub(GEN E, GEN z1, GEN z2).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltaniyama: modular parametrization computation and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: elltaniyama(E, {d = seriesprecision}) computes modular parametrization of elliptic curve E/Q returning power series [u,v] characterized by satisfying the curve equation and pullback of Néron differential equal to 2iπ f(z)dz. Algorithm assumes E is a strong Weil curve and Manin constant = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns series in variable x = exp(2iπz), prec terms. Library syntax: GEN elltaniyama(GEN E, long precdl). Be mindful of the assumption on Manin constant; results rely on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: elltatepairing: Tate pairing precondition
rubrics_metrics.description: elltatepairing(E, P, Q, m) computes the Tate pairing of P and Q on E; P must be an m-torsion point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN elltatepairing(GEN E, GEN P, GEN Q, GEN m). Ensure P has correct torsion order.

rubrics_metrics.name: elltors: torsion subgroup format
rubrics_metrics.description: elltors(E) returns torsion subgroup as [t, v1, v2] where t = order of torsion group, v1 describes structure as product of cyclic groups (decreasing order), and v2 gives generators for these cyclic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E must be ell structure output by ellinit. Example shows format [4, [2,2], [[0,0],[1,0]]]. Library syntax: GEN elltors(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltwist: twist construction and inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: elltwist(E, {P}) returns coefficients [a1,a2,a3,a4,a6] of twist of E by quadratic extension defined by P (polynomial) or quadpoly(P) when P integer; for finite fields P may be omitted to get random nontrivial twist. For number fields use minimal model if exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples for twist by discriminant −3 and Artin–Schreier twist in characteristic 2 provided. Library syntax: GEN elltwist(GEN E, GEN P = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellweilpairing: Weil pairing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: ellweilpairing(E, P, Q, m) computes the Weil pairing of m-torsion points P and Q on E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P and Q must be m-torsion. Library syntax: GEN ellweilpairing(GEN E, GEN P, GEN Q, GEN m).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellwp: Weierstrass ℘-function evaluation and options
rubrics_metrics.description: ellwp(w, {z = x}, {flag = 0}) computes ℘(z) attached to lattice w or elliptic curve E; flag=1 returns [℘(z), ℘'(z)]. Also supports series expansion around z=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts w from ellperiods; series and precision variants ellwpseries/ellwp0 exist. Library syntax: GEN ellwp0(GEN w, GEN z = NULL, long flag, long prec) and GEN ellwp(GEN w, GEN z, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellxn: division polynomials numerator/denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: ellxn(E, n, {v = x}) returns [φ_n(P), ψ_n(P)^2] which give numerator and denominator of x-coordinate of [n]P; depends only on v (x-coordinate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard notation: [n]P = (φ_n ψ_n : ω_n : ψ_n^3). Library syntax: GEN ellxn(GEN E, long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellzeta: Weierstrass ζ-function and quasi-periods
rubrics_metrics.description: ellzeta(w, {z = x}) computes ζ(z,L) for lattice w or E; quasi-periods obtained via elleta or from ζ(ω_i/2). Series expansion around z=0 supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag/quasi-period usage similar to ellperiods/ellsigma. Library syntax: GEN ellzeta(GEN w, GEN z = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellztopoint: inverse mapping z → point and behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: ellztopoint(E, z) computes coordinates [x,y] on E corresponding to complex or p-adic parameter z (inverse of ellpointtoz). For p-adic multiplicative reduction interprets z as element on Tate curve Q̄_p^*/q^Z; for complex numbers returns ℘ and derivative (with adjustments for general Weierstrass equation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If z in lattice gives point at infinity [0]. Library syntax: GEN pointell(GEN E, GEN z, long prec). Examples illustrate p-adic and complex cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: genus2red: reduction type computation and output format
rubrics_metrics.description: genus2red(PQ, {p}) determines reduction at p>2 (or all odd primes dividing discriminant if p omitted) of genus-2 curve C/Q defined by y^2=P(x) or y^2+Q(x)y=P(x); returns [N, FaN, T, V] with N conductor (local or global), FaN factorization, T minimal model over Z[1/2], and V describing reduction types at considered p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat: incomplete for p=2 — may return only odd part of conductor. When p specified V = [p, stable, red] with stable = [type, vecj] enumerating 7 types describing stable reduction and Jacobian behavior (types 1–7 with detailed meanings), and red = [NUtype, neron] where NUtype is Namikawa–Ueno symbol and neron is component group. Notes on normalization of Kodaira/Namikawa–Ueno symbols provided. Library syntax: GEN genus2red(GEN PQ, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperellcharpoly: Frobenius characteristic polynomial for hyperelliptic curves
rubrics_metrics.description: hyperellcharpoly(X) returns characteristic polynomial of Frobenius for non-singular hyperelliptic curve X over finite field, where X may be given by squarefree polynomial P (y^2=P(x)) or vector [P,Q] with Q^2+4P squarefree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN hyperellcharpoly(GEN X).

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperellpadicfrobenius: hyperelliptic Frobenius matrix and precision
rubrics_metrics.description: hyperellpadicfrobenius(Q, p, n) for curve y^2=Q(x) (degree d, p≥d, good reduction at p) returns matrix of Frobenius on D_p(X)=Q_p⊗H^1_dR(X/Q) with basis (ω,xω,...,x^{g−1}ω) computed to absolute p-adic precision p^n. Characteristic polynomial is numerator of zeta function mod p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN hyperellpadicfrobenius(GEN Q, ulong p, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: L-function definition: three assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A datum (a, a*, A, N, k, ε, r) defines an L-function if it satisfies (1) Convergence: a_n = O(n^{k1+ε}) so L(s)=∑ a_n n^{-s} converges absolutely in some right half-plane; (2) Analytic continuation: L(s) has meromorphic continuation to C with finitely many poles; (3) Functional equation: there exists integer k, complex ε and a* such that completed Λ(a,s)=N^{s/2} γ_A(s) L(a,s) satisfies Λ(a,k−s)=ε Λ(a*,s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often a*=a (self-dual) forcing |ε|=1. No assumption of multiplicativity/Euler product. These are the required mathematical standards for an object to be treated as an L-function in this package.

rubrics_metrics.name: L-function important caveat: growth exponent and experimental intent
rubrics_metrics.description: The package assumes growth exponent k1=(k−1)/2 if Λ entire and k1=k−1 otherwise, and that implied O-constants are small; this is a practical assumption that may be changed. Intended use is experimentation and conjecture formulation — numerical results are not proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should increase realbitprecision to reduce errors and treat numerical outputs as heuristic. Precision requested (in bits) has major impact on runtimes; manipulate precision via realbitprecision for finer granularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta function definition and functional equation
rubrics_metrics.description: Theta function θ(a,t) attached to L via Mellin inversion: θ(a,t) = (1/2πi)∫_{(c)} t^{-s} Λ(s) ds, with resulting series θ(a,t)=∑ a_n K(n t / N^{1/2}) and functional equation θ(a,1/t) − ε t^k θ(a*,t) = P_Λ(t), where P_Λ is polynomial from polar part of Λ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: θ-values often easier to compute than L(s); functional equation provides a fast way to guess missing invariants of L. K(t) integral and domain conditions given.

rubrics_metrics.name: L-function data structures and initialization levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Three levels: Lmath (mathematical description), Ldata (computational description containing complete datum a, a*, A, k, N, ε, r — obtained by lfuncreate), and Linit (contains Ldata plus precomputation for fast numerical computation over a fixed domain and order of derivatives — obtained by lfuninit or lfunthetainit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All functions specific to L/theta use prefix lfun and accept Lmath/Ldata/Linit as first argument. For many evaluations (plots, zero searches) construct Linit once for efficiency. If you use Linit outside its initialized domain, a warning is issued and initialization is re-done (inefficient). The package expects Ldata components to be exact when possible; missing components can be estimated but accuracy is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design problem and precision guidance for L computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Design recognizes that components of Ldata should be given exactly since required accuracy may be unbounded; but this is not always possible. Requested precision impacts runtime; routines specify precision in bits and users are advised to manipulate precision with realbitprecision for finer control (increments of 64 bits otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical results should be taken with a grain of salt: increase precision to test stability. Examples show lfuncreate/lfuninit usage and warnings when evaluating outside init domain.
